title: India Beat Sri Lanka and Uganda to Complete Commonwealth Kabaddi Double
headline: India Beat Sri Lanka and Uganda to Complete Commonwealth Kabaddi Double
subheadline: India won the men's final 54-20 over Sri Lanka and the women's final 35-15 over Uganda in Ahmedabad to claim both titles at the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship.
summary: India won the men's final 54-20 over Sri Lanka and the women's final 35-15 over Uganda in Ahmedabad to claim both titles at the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship.
excerpt: India won the men's final 54-20 over Sri Lanka and the women's final 35-15 over Uganda in Ahmedabad to claim both titles at the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship.
body:
• India won both titles at the inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship in Ahmedabad on October 31, beating Sri Lanka 54-20 in the men's final and Uganda 35-15 in the women's final.
  • Aditya Shinde scored a Super 10 with 10 raid points in the men's final, while Sakshi top-scored with nine raid points in the women's final.
  • The men's team finished unbeaten with eight wins from eight matches, scoring 380 points and conceding 193 across the tournament.
  • The women's team also finished unbeaten, winning six matches from six, including a 39-14 semi-final win over Sri Lanka.

India became the first champions of the Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship in both the men's and women's competitions on Saturday in Ahmedabad, completing a double on the final day of the inaugural tournament. The men beat Sri Lanka 54-20 after the women had beaten Uganda 35-15 earlier in the evening at the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex, according to Pro Kabaddi.

Men's final: India pull clear before half-time

India led Sri Lanka 15-8 with 10 minutes of the first half remaining, having already inflicted an All-Out. They outscored Sri Lanka 15-2 from there to lead 30-10 at half-time, with a second All-Out in the closing five minutes of the half. Sri Lanka managed two successful raids from 21 in the first half, while India's defenders made nine successful tackles from 10 attempts.

India inflicted two more All-Outs after the break and won the second half 24-10. Across the match India made 24 successful raids from 40, compared with Sri Lanka's seven from 41, and finished with 30 raid points and 14 tackle points.

Aditya Shinde top-scored for India with a Super 10, scoring 10 raid points from 14 raids, including four bonus points. Bharat Hooda added eight raid points, all in the second half, and was not tackled once in seven raids. Pankaj Mohite scored six points and vice-captain Naveen Kumar added five. Yogesh Dahiya led the defence with a High 5, making five successful tackles from five attempts, all in the first half.

Maduwantha was Sri Lanka's top scorer with six tackle points, including two Super Tackles, while Ansaf and Viduranga added three points each. Sri Lanka finished with 11 raid points and nine tackle points and failed in seven of their nine do-or-die raids.

"With more and more tournaments being held, it's great for the people of Ahmedabad too, and we received so much support from them."

— Aditya Shinde, India raider

Women's final: Sakshi leads unbeaten run

In the women's final, India led Uganda 7-3 with 10 minutes of the first half remaining before outscoring them 15-4, including an All-Out, to lead 22-7 at half-time. A second All-Out, with less than 10 minutes to play, put the result beyond doubt.

Sakshi top-scored for India with nine raid points from 10 raids, including two bonus points, with seven of those points coming in the first half. Anu added six raid points and captain Nidhi Sharma five, including three bonus points. Ritu and Suman anchored the defence with four tackle points each. India scored 20 raid points and 10 tackle points and inflicted two All-Outs.

Nakayongo Shirat carried Uganda's attack, making 24 of their 35 raids and scoring 11 of their 15 points, including three bonus points. Uganda's other raiders managed three points between them.

Sakshi finished the championship with 52 points from six matches. India Women opened with a 73-13 win over Malaysia, then beat Singapore 32-16, Uganda 41-18 and Nigeria 38-10 to finish top of Group A, before beating Sri Lanka 39-14 in the semi-final.

What the double means

The men's title capped a perfect campaign of eight wins from eight matches. India topped Group A with six wins, beating England 46-26, Uganda 44-30, Malaysia 37-23, Nigeria 50-23, Tanzania 48-20 and Sri Lanka 45-24, then beat Bangladesh 56-27 in the semi-final. No opponent scored more than 30 points against them in the tournament.

Both finals were played on Day 9 of the championship in Ahmedabad. The sources read for this report do not state a next fixture for either Indian team after the championship.
